11. Hypochlorite bleaches are cleaning products containing the hypochlorite ion, ClO−(aq), a good oxidising agent.

(c)

In one method that can be used to measure the concentration of hypochlorite ions in a sample of bleach, the bleach sample is reacted with excess hydrogen peroxide.

H2O2(aq) + ClO−(aq) → H2O(ℓ) + Cl−(aq) + O2(g)

By measuring the volume of oxygen given off, the concentration of bleach can be calculated.

(ii)

80 cm3 of oxygen gas was produced from 5·0 cm3 of bleach.

H2O2(aq) + ClO−(aq) → H2O(ℓ) + Cl−(aq) + O2(g)

Calculate the concentration of hypochlorite ion, in mol l−1, in bleach.

Take the molar volume of one mole of oxygen to be 24 litres.

Units are not required but must be correct if given. (Wrong units would only be penalised once in any paper).
